_comment: The reference map of the optional Ice and Fire hooks of Spider Queen: Hungry Craft (Necromancy IV round 4/5).
It is written by hand on purpose: the only hook of this mod that names a VANILLA member is
EntityDragonBaseRiderMixin, which injects into Entity#getControllingPassenger - a method that Ice and Fire only
overrides, so its name in a published jar is the SRG name m_6688_ while a development workspace calls it
getControllingPassenger. Mixin can only bridge that with a reference map, and the reference map of the main
configuration cannot carry it: that file is generated from the Minecraft mappings, which do not know the class of
another mod. So the entries are written here, keyed exactly the way Mixin resolves the member - the official name
and descriptor on the left, the SRG name on the right - and the file is declared by
spiderqueen_hungrycraft_iaf.mixins.json and by IceAndFireMixinPlugin#getRefMapperConfig.
ROUND 5 - why the descriptor is part of the key, and why there are two owner forms:
* the @Inject of the rider hook now names the full descriptor
(getControllingPassenger()Lnet/minecraft/world/entity/LivingEntity;) because a BARE name gives Mixin nothing to
look up in this map: the translation of a member name is keyed by the complete reference, so a bare name stayed
official, the search ran against the SRG named class and found nothing
(InvalidInjectionException: could not find any targets matching 'getControllingPassenger'),
* the same member is listed twice, once with the class Ice and Fire overrides it in (EntityDragonBase) and once
with the class that declares it in the game (Entity). Mixin resolves the owner of an overridden member either
way depending on how it found the target, both classes carry m_6688_, and an entry that is never asked for costs
nothing - so both forms are stated and neither has to be guessed at run time.
The two other hooks of that configuration (EnumDragonTexturesMixin and EntityDragonBaseEyesMixin) are declared
remap = false and target methods of Ice and Fire itself, whose names are identical in both worlds: they need no
entry and deliberately have none.
For a DEVELOPMENT run with Ice and Fire installed, gradle/mixin-refmap.srg carries the same member the other way
round (m_6688_ -> getControllingPassenger), which is what mixin.env.remapRefMap asks for.
